cards.front: gravity
cards.back: A force that pulls objects towards the centre of Earth.
cards.say: gravity. A force that pulls objects towards the centre of Earth.

cards.front: force
cards.back: A push or a pull. It is measured in newtons.
cards.say: force. A push or a pull. It is measured in newtons.

cards.front: newton
cards.back: The unit of force. Its symbol is a capital N.
cards.say: newton. The unit of force. Its symbol is a capital N.

cards.front: mass
cards.back: The amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms or grams.
cards.say: mass. The amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms or grams.

cards.front: weight
cards.back: The pull of gravity on an object's mass. It is a force, so it is measured in newtons.
cards.say: weight. The pull of gravity on an object's mass. It is a force, so it is measured in newtons.

cards.front: What do we use to measure weight?
cards.back: A forcemeter, also called a newtonmeter or spring balance.
cards.say: What do we use to measure weight? A forcemeter, also called a newtonmeter or spring balance.

cards.front: What do we use to measure mass?
cards.back: A balance or scales, in kilograms or grams.
cards.say: What do we use to measure mass? A balance or scales, in kilograms or grams.

cards.front: Does your mass change on the Moon?
cards.back: No. You are still made of the same amount of matter.
cards.say: Does your mass change on the Moon? No. You are still made of the same amount of matter.

cards.front: Does your weight change on the Moon?
cards.back: Yes. It is less, because the Moon's gravity is weaker than Earth's.
cards.say: Does your weight change on the Moon? Yes. It is less, because the Moon's gravity is weaker than Earth's.

cards.front: How strong is the Moon's gravity compared with Earth's?
cards.back: About one sixth as strong.
cards.say: How strong is the Moon's gravity compared with Earth's? About one sixth as strong.

cards.front: About what weight does a mass of one kilogram have on Earth?
cards.back: About ten newtons.
cards.say: About what weight does a mass of one kilogram have on Earth? About ten newtons.

cards.front: About what weight does a mass of three kilograms have on Earth?
cards.back: About thirty newtons.
cards.say: About what weight does a mass of three kilograms have on Earth? About thirty newtons.

cards.front: About what weight does a 100 gram apple have on Earth?
cards.back: About one newton.
cards.say: About what weight does a one hundred gram apple have on Earth? About one newton.

cards.front: In which direction does gravity pull?
cards.back: Downwards, towards the centre of Earth.
cards.say: In which direction does gravity pull? Downwards, towards the centre of Earth.

cards.front: Why does a dropped ball come down?
cards.back: Gravity pulls it towards Earth.
cards.say: Why does a dropped ball come down? Gravity pulls it towards Earth.

cards.front: Without air, do heavy and light objects drop at the same rate?
cards.back: Yes. In a vacuum they drop at the same rate. Air resistance is why a feather drops slowly in air.
cards.say: Without air, do heavy and light objects drop at the same rate? Yes. In a vacuum they drop at the same rate. Air resistance is why a feather drops slowly in air.

cards.front: Which has stronger gravity, Jupiter or Earth?
cards.back: Jupiter. An object would weigh more there.
cards.say: Which has stronger gravity, Jupiter or Earth? Jupiter. An object would weigh more there.

cards.front: What happens to a spring in a forcemeter when you hang a heavier object?
cards.back: The spring stretches more, and the pointer shows a larger force.
cards.say: What happens to a spring in a forcemeter when you hang a heavier object? The spring stretches more, and the pointer shows a larger force.

cards.front: Is mass measured in newtons?
cards.back: No. Mass is measured in kilograms. Newtons measure force, such as weight.
cards.say: Is mass measured in newtons? No. Mass is measured in kilograms. Newtons measure force, such as weight.

cards.front: Does gravity need to touch an object to pull it?
cards.back: No. Gravity is a non-contact force that acts at a distance.
cards.say: Does gravity need to touch an object to pull it? No. Gravity is a non-contact force that acts at a distance.

cards.front: Why is Earth's pull on us so strong?
cards.back: Earth has a huge mass. The bigger the mass, the stronger its gravity.
cards.say: Why is Earth's pull on us so strong? Earth has a huge mass. The bigger the mass, the stronger its gravity.
